analysis.summary: Accent Microcell Ltd hosted an earnings conference call on May 16, 2026, to present its operating and financial performance for FY26. Total sales volumes achieved reached 15,000 metric tons against an installed manufacturing capacity of approximately 10,000 metric tons, supported by an increase in trading volumes and high-value premium products such as MCC Spheres and SMCC. Commercialization of Unit 3 Phase 1 was delayed due to abnormal monsoons and regulatory/environmental approvals, but commercial production is expected to begin shortly after remaining approvals are received. Phase 2 expansion for MCC capacity is planned for tentative launch around March 2027 and will be funded through rights issue proceeds and internal accruals. guidance.claim: Phase 1 of Unit 3 will launch much earlier than Phase 2.
guidance.quote: Phase 1 will be launched, much earlier than Phase 2.

guidance.claim: Unit 3 Phase 1 is expected to generate peak capacity revenue of around Rs 150 crores.
guidance.quote: At peak capacity, we are assuming revenue of around, 150 crores.

guidance.claim: Unit 3 Phase 1 at peak capacity is expected to generate revenue equal to roughly 40% of the existing revenue from Unit 1 and Unit 2.
guidance.quote: Phase 1, at a peak capacity, say, will fetch, revenue of around, roughly between, say, 40% of the, say, existing revenue that would be from Unit 1 and 2.

guidance.claim: Premium products are expected to represent roughly 16 to 17% of total revenue for FY27.
guidance.quote: Gradually, it is going to increase, but for H2 or for entire finance year 27, it's going to be, say, more or less 16 to 17%.

guidance.claim: Management expects Unit 3 Phase 2 to go live around March 2027.
guidance.quote: Phase 2, say, it will be premature for me to give any kind of an exact deadline, but as of now, we are expecting it to go live in the month of, March 27.

guidance.claim: Accent Microcell projects ₹70 crore in revenue in Year 1 from its Unit-III expansion.
The expected revenue mix for Unit-III is 60% exports and 40% domestic sales.
Management expects the company to achieve a revenue CAGR of 15 to 20% over the next 3 to 5 years.
guidance.quote: Just a moment, sir, at least say 15 to 20% CAGR for next 3 to 5 years. We are expecting.

guidance.claim: Management expects Phase 1 capacity utilization to be around 60% in its first full year of operation.
guidance.quote: I won't be able to quantify in terms of financial figure, but yes, from the from current fiscal given a full year capacity, we are expecting it to be utility level, to be around 60% for the 1st year.

demand_outlook.claim: Management considers the current demand outlook for MCC to be good based on the company's existing order book.
demand_outlook.quote: So, currency, current, MCC demand outlook is good, taking into account our existing order book.

demand_outlook.claim: The company has roughly 4,000 metric tons of orders on hand across domestic and export markets.
demand_outlook.quote: Taking into account, say, domestic and export market, we have roughly around, 4,000 metric tons orders on hand with us.

demand_outlook.claim: Management does not foresee competition challenges in the overall MCC or excipients market.
demand_outlook.quote: we don't foresee any kind of competition when it comes to, say, overall MCC market, or in general, excipients range of products.

demand_outlook.claim: The company has export and domestic order books on hand for at least 3 to 4 months.
demand_outlook.quote: for, at least for 3 to 4 months, we have ordered books on hand for export and domestic markets.

demand_outlook.claim: Management projects global MCC demand growth to increase by an additional 1 to 1.5% above the baseline CAGR of 5 to 6%.
demand_outlook.quote: Yes, sir, currently. if we talk about CAGR, so about 5 to 6% and upcoming times, at least for a couple of years, that would be. We are expecting to increase at least one to 1.5% more

demand_outlook.claim: The global market demand for MCC is around 250,000 metric tons, while Indian domestic demand stands at 50,000 metric tons per annum.
demand_outlook.quote: We have 2.5 lakh is globally 50,000 metric ton for the Indian market.

demand_outlook.claim: Product inquiries have increased following an operational incident at a peer manufacturing plant.
demand_outlook.quote: of course is, there has been product. Inquiry has been increased, and we have been taking care of the business from our business side.

capex_expansion.claim: Phase 1 will cater to premium excipient products while Phase 2 will cater to MCC.
capex_expansion.quote: Phase 1 will cater to, say, a premium range of excipient products, and Phase 2 will cater to MCC.

capex_expansion.claim: The company has acquired land capable of accommodating expansion up to Phase 6.
capex_expansion.quote: we have purchased land for till phase 6.

capex_expansion.claim: Phase 3 is tentatively expected to start around 2028 following success in Phase 2.
capex_expansion.quote: Almost in 2028 will start the Phase 3.

capex_expansion.claim: Phase 1 has a combined installed capacity of 2,400 metric tons across three planned products.
capex_expansion.quote: total 2,400 Metrick ton capacity we have, taking into account the combination of all the three products, depending upon the market scenario and the response from, we receive from the customer.

capex_expansion.claim: Total capex for Unit 3 Phase 1 and Phase 2 excluding land is estimated to be between INR 105 crore and 110 crore.
capex_expansion.quote: so, I can share you the say, rough idea about the total capex for entire unit 3 as of now, that is phase 1 phase 2, except the land portion, I think. It will be around say, it will be anywhere between 105 to 110 cr.

capex_expansion.claim: Commercial production for Unit 3 Phase 1 is expected by late October or the first couple of weeks of November 2025.
capex_expansion.quote: Yes, sir. By say, quarter 3 of the current financial year. So anywhere between, say by the end of October or in the 1st couple of weeks of November.

capex_expansion.claim: Trial runs for Unit 3 Phase 2 are expected to begin in July 2026, with Phase 2 capex estimated at INR 55 to 60 crore excluding land.
capex_expansion.quote: Sir, we're expecting it to be in the month of say, July 2,026.

margins_costs.claim: Any nominal cost increase in imported wood pulp raw material has been passed on completely to customers.
margins_costs.quote: Sir, whatever the, say, nominal increase in the cost, for the import of raw material that is wood pulp has been completely passed on through the customer.

margins_costs.claim: The company's gross profit margin stands at approximately 38%.
margins_costs.quote: gross profit percentage is around 38%, so I guess, more or less, your concern, or rather, the question will be answered through that percentage.

margins_costs.claim: Trading activities yield margins of 4-5% compared to overall blended profit margins.
margins_costs.quote: Trading margins are 4-5%, as compared to the, blended profit margins that what you are seeing in the phase of the profit and loss account.

margins_costs.claim: Selling prices for CMC are approximately Rs 400 per kg domestically and Rs 800 to Rs 900 per kg in export markets.
margins_costs.quote: Yes, in domestic selling price of CMC is almost Rs 400Kg and for foreign its selling price will be Rs 800 to 900Kg for export.

margins_costs.claim: Blended profit margins are expected to increase by at least 2 to 3 percentage points due to higher sales of premium products.
margins_costs.quote: it is prudent enough to assume that the blended profit margins are going to increase by, say, at least 2-3 percentage.

margins_costs.claim: EBITDA for FY26 reached Rs. 6,345.83 Lakhs, up 31.34% YoY from Rs. 4,831.77 Lakhs in FY25.
EBITDA margin stood at 18.18% in FY26 compared to 18.26% in FY25.
PAT margin reached 12.57% for FY26 compared to 12.50% in FY25.
The price of Croscarmellose Sodium is approximately 3.5 times that of Microcrystalline Cellulose.
margins_costs.quote: The price of CC. CCS is around 3.5 times of MCC.

margins_costs.claim: MCC realization stands at around INR 230 per kg for export markets and INR 180 per kg for the domestic market.
margins_costs.quote: Sir. For export markets around 2 30 per kg. And for domestic is around 1 80 per kg.

margins_costs.claim: Superior grade Sapi bulk raw material costs between INR 80 to 85 compared to INR 60 for Riya grade.
margins_costs.quote: Let's take a hypothetical example. If the price of riya is around ₹60. Price of, say, I, converted into INR. The price of sapi will run anywhere between 80 to 85.

orders_capacity.claim: Installed capacity for both operating plants is roughly 10,000 metric tons.
orders_capacity.quote: Yeah, and the installed capacity for both the plant is roughly around 10,000 metric ton.

orders_capacity.claim: Total sales volume achieved in FY26 was 15,000 metric tons.
Roughly 70% of total volume was fulfilled through manufactured capacity and 25-30% was from traded volumes.
orders_capacity.quote: around, say, 70% of the, say, total, export, or rather, the capacity utilization was from the manufacturing capacity, and roughly 25-30% was from the traded volumes.

orders_capacity.claim: The company has approximately 100 metric tons per month capacity for MCC Spheres.
orders_capacity.quote: say, we have, say, around, 100 metric ton capacity for MCC Spears

orders_capacity.claim: The Pirana facility has an installed capacity of 2,000 MTPA.
Pirana facility capacity utilization operated at 100%.
The Dahej SEZ facility has an installed capacity of 7,200 MTPA.
Dahej SEZ facility capacity utilization operated at 95%.
The company currently holds 4 to 5 months of business orders on hand.
orders_capacity.quote: Yes, we have at present about, you can say for 4 to 5 months. We have business on hand, and that's why. Actually, we are also coming up with phase 2 for unit 3.

orders_capacity.claim: Total installed capacity will reach 24,000 metric tons per annum following the completion of Phase 1 and Phase 2 of Unit 3.
orders_capacity.quote: So it will. Total will be 24,000 metric ton per annum.

orders_capacity.claim: The company's current installed manufacturing capacity is 9,600 metric tons per annum.
orders_capacity.quote: 9,600 is our current capacity, so our phase? One, is about 2,400.

capital_allocation.claim: Phase 2 expansion will be funded via rights issue proceeds and internal accruals.
capital_allocation.quote: Phase 2, Phase 2, we are going to fund it out from right issue, and to a certain extent, internal equals.

capital_allocation.claim: Management foresees no additional borrowing requirements for working capital.
capital_allocation.quote: And for working capital, we… as of now, we don't foresee any kind of further borrowing requirements.

capital_allocation.claim: Management expects internal accruals to meet future phase expansion needs without debt.
capital_allocation.quote: I think, the internal accruals will suffice the requirement. As of now, we don't see any kind of such debt requirements.

capital_allocation.claim: The company has not planned any debt fundraising for Phase 1 and Phase 2.
capital_allocation.quote: Sir, for, Phase 1 and Phase 2, we have not, yet planned any kind of an, say, fundraising through debt, because it will be, say, partially funded out of internet growth, and, balance will be from right issue.

capital_allocation.claim: Fixed assets increased to Rs. 15,607.80 Lakhs as of March 31, 2026, from Rs. 6,232.48 Lakhs as of March 31, 2025.
Reserves and surplus grew to Rs. 25,149.56 Lakhs as of March 31, 2026, compared to Rs. 17,374.97 Lakhs as of March 31, 2025.
The company raised approximately INR 40 crore through a rights issue to fund its expansion plans.
capital_allocation.quote: Apart from that. Just to be clear for the fund raising that what you have done for the right issue. It is around 40 crores, and the total cost of phase 2 will be around roughly between 55 to 60 crores.

capital_allocation.claim: Adjacent land was purchased from promoter entities for INR 6 crore to build a new warehouse for inventory storage.
capital_allocation.quote: Sir, land was purchased from the parties that you stated for which due to the lack of the say inventory, for which inventory storage was required. Say, we have, build up a new go down as well. Warehouse as well on the land that is purchased by the companies.

risks_headwinds.claim: Unit 3 Phase 1 was delayed due to two consecutive abnormal monsoons and regulatory licensing requirements for greenfield projects.
risks_headwinds.quote: The delay in Phase 1 was, primarily due to two reasons, two back-to-back abnormal monsoons, and, certain licensing work, read with, say, regulatory approvals that was required, being, project treated as, greenfield.

risks_headwinds.claim: Geopolitical tensions caused challenges related to transit times rather than raw material price fluctuations.
risks_headwinds.quote: Sir in this the situation is that due to geopolitical tension there is no fluctuation in prices. Whatever delay there is and whatever challenges there are they are related to transit time to the extent what you have understood so far.

risks_headwinds.claim: On-site execution activities for Unit-III were impacted by two consecutive abnormal monsoon seasons.
Obtaining required regulatory approvals involved extended liaisoning timelines.
risks_headwinds.quote: Extended liaisoning timelines for obtaining the required regulatory approvals

risks_headwinds.claim: Debtor days increased because the company offered longer payment terms to onboard Indian MNC pharmaceutical customers.
risks_headwinds.quote: Sir, that data needs to be read with, the say, certain percentage decrease in the export sales as well, because we have started targeting Indian MNCs wherein to enter or to have a competitive edge. Labor payment terms have been offered by the company.

risks_headwinds.claim: There is currently no clarity regarding tariff policies for the pharmaceutical sector.
risks_headwinds.quote: Sir, as of now, to the extent would you understand? There is no clarity regarding tariff for the Pharma sector.
